issues.legal_issue: A contract for the sale of jointly owned property may be specifically enforced against the contracting co-owner’s identifiable share when that co-owner lacked authority to bind the other owner.
material_facts: The agreement covered the whole property, which was owned in equal shares by the contracting seller and his sister.
The seller purported to contract on his sister’s behalf but had no authority to do so.
The seller’s own share was identifiable, and the purchasers sought specific performance limited to that share.
issues.conclusion: Section 12 applied because the agreement covered the whole property but the seller could not perform the part relating to his sister’s share. Specific performance could therefore be granted against the seller’s share, subject to the purchasers satisfying the requirements for partial performance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 12(2) and 12(3) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, specific performance of the performable part may be granted when the defendant cannot perform the whole contract and the statutory conditions for partial performance are met. Kartar Singh v. Harjinder Singh was confined to its facts: there, the non-signing co-owner had not contracted at all and the contracting party’s agreement to sell his own share was separate and severable. It does not establish that Section 12 is inapplicable whenever a co-owner lacks authority to sell another owner’s share. Rachakonda Narayana v. Ponthala Parvathamma explains the conditions for partial performance.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and agreement_covers_multiple_owners_shares and seller_lacks_authority_for_another_share and seller_owns_identifiable_share and purchaser_accepts_performable_share and purchaser_relinquishes_remaining_performance_and_compensation

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A party seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.agreement_covers_multiple_owners_shares: The agreement purports to cover shares owned by more than one person.
predicates.seller_lacks_authority_for_another_share: The person who made the agreement lacked authority to bind another owner as to that owner’s share.
predicates.seller_owns_identifiable_share: The contracting seller owns a share that can be distinguished from the other owner’s share.
predicates.purchaser_accepts_performable_share: The purchaser seeks performance only of the part the seller can perform.
predicates.purchaser_relinquishes_remaining_perform: The purchaser gives up any claim to performance of the unperformable part and any claim to compensation for its non-performance.

issues.definition: When an agreement covers multiple owners’ shares, the seller lacks authority over another share, the seller’s own share is identifiable, and the purchaser accepts performance limited to that share while relinquishing the other claims, specific performance may be enforced against the seller’s share.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser may satisfy the requirement to relinquish claims to the unperformable part of a contract and compensation at a late stage of litigation, including by an amended prayer and an unequivocal statement in court.
material_facts: The purchasers sought to amend their requested relief to limit it to the seller’s share.
Their amended request did not seek performance of the other owner’s share or compensation for its non-performance.
Their counsel stated that they relinquished any claim for damages and would not press their cross-objection.
The amendment and statement were made after the litigation had reached the appellate stage.
issues.conclusion: The relinquishment could be made at that stage and did not have to be specifically pleaded in prescribed words. The amended request, read as a whole, and the statement in court sufficiently established relinquishment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(ii) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires relinquishment of claims to performance of the remaining part and compensation for the defendant’s default, but does not impose a time limit for doing so. Rachakonda Narayana v. Ponthala Parvathamma and Surjit Kaur v. Naurata Singh recognize that an application to relinquish claims may be made at the appellate stage. Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar holds that relinquishment may be made at any stage of the litigation. The court must read the amendment as a whole, and an unequivocal statement in court may establish relinquishment.

predicates.partial_specific_performance_proceeding: A party seeks specific performance limited to the part of an agreement that the other party can perform.
predicates.purchaser_limits_requested_relief_to_per: The purchaser amends or states the requested relief to cover only the performable part.
predicates.purchaser_abandons_remaining_performance: The purchaser gives up the claim to performance of the part that cannot be performed.
predicates.purchaser_disclaims_compensation: The purchaser expressly or by necessary implication gives up compensation for the default.

issues.definition: If a purchaser seeking partial performance limits the requested relief to the performable part and gives up both the remaining performance claim and compensation, the relinquishment may satisfy the requirement even when made late in the litigation.

issues.legal_issue: The discretionary decision to grant specific performance may favor the purchasers despite their long-term occupation as tenants and unpaid rent when the seller induced their belief that he could contract for the whole property and the delay was not their fault.
material_facts: The seller represented that he had authority to contract for the other co-owner’s share, but that representation was incorrect.
The purchasers had paid amounts toward the transaction, and the delay in completing the sale was not attributed to them.
The purchasers occupied the property as tenants and had not paid rent for a long period.
Any claim for rent arrears could be determined in a separate proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances favored specific performance of the seller’s share rather than refusal of relief. The unpaid-rent claim did not require refusing specific performance and could be pursued separately.
issues.legal_principle: Discretionary relief must be exercised reasonably in light of the circumstances of each case. The court considered the purchasers’ payments, the seller’s misleading representation about his authority, the fact that the purchasers were not responsible for the delay, and the availability of a separate proceeding to determine rent arrears.

rule.if: specific_performance_appeal and seller_misrepresented_authority_over_other_share and purchasers_paid_toward_transaction and delay_not_attributable_to_purchasers and occupants_have_unpaid_rent and rent_claim_can_be_separately_decided

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a request for specific performance.
predicates.seller_misrepresented_authority_over_oth: The seller led the purchasers to believe he could contract for another owner’s share when he could not.
predicates.purchasers_paid_toward_transaction: The purchasers paid amounts toward the agreed sale transaction.
predicates.delay_not_attributable_to_purchasers: The purchasers were not responsible for the delay in completing the sale.
predicates.occupants_have_unpaid_rent: The purchasers occupied the property as tenants and had not paid rent.
predicates.rent_claim_can_be_separately_decided: A claim for unpaid rent can be determined in a separate proceeding.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance appeal involves a seller who misrepresented his authority, purchasers who paid toward the transaction and did not cause the delay, and unpaid rent that can be decided separately, the circumstances may favor granting specific performance despite the rent arrears.
